newsitem.title: USA: Sketches of main players in Oklahoma bombing case.
newsitem.headline: Sketches of main players in Oklahoma bombing case.

text.p: Following are the major players in the Oklahoma City bombing trial that began with jury selection on March 31 and proceeds with opening statements on Thursday.

-- Timothy McVeigh, 29 and a Gulf War veteran, is charged in the bombing with former Army buddy Terry Nichols. The two will be tried separately. Prosecutors say they turned against the government during the 1993 standoff between the FBI and the Branch Davidian sect in Waco, Texas. McVeigh left the Army in late 1991 and returned to his native western New York where he worked as a security guard in Buffalo. In 1993 he became a drifter, doing odd jobs and selling guns. The tall, lanky McVeigh is considered bright and has appeared animated during pre-trial hearings and jury selection.

-- U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch, 66, was appointed in 1974 by President Richard Nixon. Matsch generally is respected by prosecutors and defence attorneys, although they incur his sharp rebukes as he maintains iron-handed control of his courtroom.

In 1987, he sentenced two white supremacists to 150 years each in prison in the murder of Denver radio talk show host Alan Berg, a Jew. He was assigned to the bombing case after an appeals court disqualified an Oklahoma City judge. He was born in Burlington, Iowa.

-- The government's lead prosecutor is Joseph Hartzler, 46, who has spent all but four years of his career as a Justice Department attorney. In Chicago he won convictions for seditious conspiracy of four people who sought independence for Puerto Rico and of a county judge in a corruption case.
He graduated first in his law school class at American University. He was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 1989 and uses a motorized scooter. He was born in Columbus, Ohio.

-- McVeigh's lead attorney, Stephen Jones, has represented other unpopular defendants and causes in his 31 years of law practice, handling 25 death-penalty cases and a lawsuit against substandard prisons. He served four years as general counsel of the American Civil Liberties Union Oklahoma affiliate. He also has been a prosecutor. A Republican, he ran unsuccessfully for the U.S. Senate and for attorney general of Oklahoma, his adopted state.
The 56-year-old attorney was born in Lafayette, Louisiana.

-- Michael Fortier, 28, will be a key witness for the prosecution. He was a friend of McVeigh from the army and lived in Kingman, Arizona. Fortier has pleaded guilty to four felony accounts in return for testifying that he knew about plans for the bombing but did nothing to stop it. He is expected to testify that he and McVeigh drove to Oklahoma City where McVeigh told him the Alfed P. Murrah federal building was the target. He faces up to 23 years in prison.

-- Lori Fortier, Michael Fortier's wife, is also expected to testify for the prosecution. Her husband's agreement to testify in exchange for a lesser charge also allowed her to escape prosecution. She is expected to testify about a phony South Dakota driver's license McVeigh allegedly made for himself bearing the name Robert Kling, an alias the government says McVeigh used.
